assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. This is a rare chain from basic hormone biology to a major, widely used medicine; originality, clarity and clinical impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and the biologically active GLP-1 peptide forms, Drucker the intestinotrophic and receptor biology and the road to therapy, and Knudsen the development of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's early peptide work is real but contested and would be left out of a three-person configuration, which is a sensitive allocation of credit; the Habener lab contribution is not listed in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed repeatedly and independently over decades, with mature randomized outcome data. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing given global impact.
uncertainties: Fair apportioning of credit among Mojsov, Habener-group work and the three proposed laureates is disputed and my recollection of the details is not independently verified.
Long-term safety and durability of effects on obesity are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and a core principle of proteostasis, now relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually original, clean and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily elucidated the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 pathway, a natural two-person configuration. Credit is comparatively unambiguous, though other early contributors such as Kozutsumi and Sidrauski/Ron on the PERK arm exist outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across species with mechanistic clarity; the discovery has been recognised by major prizes. Clinical translation is still emerging, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Translational impact in human disease is less established than the basic biology.
Possible competing claims for the PERK/ATF6 arms; not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with multiple approved products. Originality and clinical impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed the clinically successful CAR designs with costimulatory domains; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Eshhar, Brentjens and others outside the supplied credit also contributed foundational ideas, so any configuration is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapies since 2017 with multi-year follow-up. Extension to solid tumours and safety issues remain open, but the core achievement is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Allocation among June, Sadelain, Rosenberg and non-listed pioneers is unresolved.
Toxicity and limited efficacy in solid tumours.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has reshaped systems neuroscience and begun to inform therapy, for example in vision restoration. It is an exceptional methodological invention.
assessment.attribution: Bamberg and Nagel identified and characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth and Boyden established neuronal use; Hegemann and Miesenboeck have strong claims too. Six credited names against a three-person limit makes this the hardest attribution problem on my ballot.
assessment.maturity: Broadly adopted and independently replicated for over a decade. Timing is appropriate, although therapeutic outcomes remain limited.
uncertainties: Large unresolved credit dispute; any trio omits significant contributors.
Fit with Medicine rather than Chemistry or Physics prize domains is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, which dramatically changed a fatal childhood disease. It is a clear case of mechanism-based therapy for a genetic neurological disorder.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis. Contributions of others in the field exist beyond the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of real-world follow-up, enabling newborn screening. Recognition is timely, though possibly slightly early relative to other antisense or RNA therapeutics.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as discovery or drug development.
Credit relative to other antisense and splicing pioneers is not fully verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and turned CML into a chronic disease. Its impact on oncology drug development is paradigmatic.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the chemistry and target programme, Druker the clinical translation, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The configuration is fair but the underlying Rowley, Nowell and Hungerford discoveries and Ciba-Geigy chemists make credit layered.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with long-term survival data. It has been widely recognised by Lasker and other prizes, and the delay in Nobel recognition raises questions about whether it is a drug-development prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier chromosome and oncogene Nobel-recognised work.
Dispute over relative roles of industry and academic contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identification as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing has implications for cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression, and is a major conceptual advance in cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and is the clearest decisive contributor; Sabatini and Schreiber identified mammalian mTOR and the rapamycin-FKBP12 target. Brown, and Heitman, Movva and Hall's early work also matter, so credit beyond Hall is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed over three decades. Clinical translation via rapalogs is real but partial.
uncertainties: Whether the laureate set should be Hall alone or include mammalian mTOR identifiers.
Controversy around some credited individuals not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids, building on Lgr5 stem cell identification, created a broadly adopted platform for studying tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised therapeutic testing.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the driving intellectual contributor; Sato executed the founding intestinal organoid experiments. A two-name configuration is plausible; Clevers' Lgr5 work and Barker's contributions are partly outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted within about fifteen years; clinical impact is still developing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical translational impact is not yet well established.
Overlap with existing stem cell prizes.
